title: Worship in a City With No Temple
text_faithful: Faith view: Revelation 21:22 says the seer saw no temple in the city, 'for the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are its temple.' In this faith reading, worship needs no separate temple building because God's presence itself is the meeting place. This is a faith statement about the vision, not a claim about any building that exists or has been built.
engineering: Engineering view: no temple building is specified, measured, or claimed as built in this record. A worship space in any real design would still need ordinary architectural decisions — capacity, acoustics, access, light, and safety — and none of those are settled by the verse. The engineering section therefore records only that the faith text removes a temple from the vision, and that any physical gathering space remains a separate design question.
body:
Revelation 21:22 presents a city with no temple building. The chapter has already described the city in detail — wall, gates, foundations, street — and then, at the point where a reader might expect a temple at the centre, the text says there is none, because the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are its temple. This record reads that verse as a deliberate reversal: in the older Jerusalem the temple was the place of presence, and here presence itself takes that role. Worship in this reading is therefore not tied to one building, one room, or one ritual site. The record keeps that reading labeled as faith throughout, and it does not turn the verse into a building plan.

Science proof: not applicable — No science proof applies to this record: it is a faith reading of a vision text, and a scientific proof of a theological claim would mislabel the kind of statement it is. The verifiable content is textual — the verse, its wording, and its place in the chapter — and that is what the demo checks.

Mathematics: The demo counts the vision's named structures: twelve gates, twelve foundations, one street, and zero temples, and reports the worship-site count the verse implies.

In this faith reading, adornment is covenant language: the city is presented as beloved, prepared, and made ready, not as a building decorated for display. The beauty language speaks of relationship and readiness, and the record does not convert it into a materials specification.

The bride image opens Revelation 21 and returns at 21:9, where an angel shows the seer 'the bride, the wife of the Lamb' and what is shown is a city. That substitution — a person-image resolved into a place — is the point of the symbol: the city stands for a people made ready. Adornment in the passage is preparation language, the same register as a wedding party preparing a bride, applied to a whole community. Readers across traditions have taken the image in that covenant sense, and this record follows that reading while naming it as a faith reading.

Science proof: not applicable — No science proof applies: the record interprets a symbol in a vision text. Its checkable content is the text itself — the two bride passages and the city they resolve into — verified by the demo's count of the passages and their verses.

title: The Twelve Tribes and Twelve Apostles, Names
text_faithful: Faith view: Revelation 21:12-14 names twelve gates inscribed with the names of the twelve tribes of Israel, and twelve foundations inscribed with the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb. In this faith reading, the two twelves hold the older covenant people and the apostolic witnesses together in one wall: the city is entered through Israel's tribes and founded on the apostles. The record names the pattern as faith symbolism and does not claim a settled list where the text itself gives none.
engineering: Engineering view: the gates and foundations here are symbolic counts, not construction quantities. Twelve gates and twelve foundations are recorded as the text's numbers, and any design that uses them would treat them as a brief — twelve of each, three per side for the gates — while the naming question stays in the faith column, where tradition, not engineering, supplies candidate lists.
body:
Revelation 21:12-14 gives the wall's two inscriptions without listing the names. The twelve tribes are the traditional sons of Israel named across the Hebrew scriptures, and the twelve apostles are the Lamb's apostles named in the Gospels and Acts. Because Revelation does not enumerate either list, traditions differ on details — for example, whether the tribal list follows the sons of Jacob or the tribal allotments, and how the apostolic list treats Judas and Matthias. This record therefore gives the structure (twelve and twelve, gates and foundations) as the text's own content, and names the lists as traditional, not as textually enumerated. That distinction is the record's main factual contribution.

title: Glory of God as Light, Faith Reading
text_faithful: Faith view: Revelation 21:23 says the city does not need sun or moon to shine on it, 'for the glory of God gives it light, and the Lamb is its lamp.' In this faith reading, light is glory made visible: God's presence is the city's illumination, and the Lamb is named as its lamp. The record keeps that as faith language about divine presence, not as a lighting specification and not as a claim that any physical light source has been built or demonstrated.
engineering: Engineering view: ordinary lighting can be described with ordinary quantities — luminous flux in lumens, area in square metres, illuminance in lux — and the demo does exactly that for a small gathering space, as an illustration of how lighting is measured. That illustration is kept strictly separate from the faith claim: it measures lamps, not glory, and it proves nothing about the vision.
body:
Light is the vision's most repeated image: the city shines like a precious jewel in 21:11, needs no sun or moon in 21:23, and has no night in 22:5. The passage moves from created lights to uncreated light, and the record reads that movement as theology — presence replacing provision — rather than as optics. Companion pairs in the suite catalog real lighting approaches (LED arrays, control systems, radiance models) under their own feasibility labels; this record does not borrow their feasibility for the faith claim.

Science proof (ordinary lighting only): illuminance equals luminous flux divided by area. A 4,000-lumen source over a 20-square-metre room gives 200 lux, a normal reading level; doubling the flux doubles the illuminance. This proves only how lamps are measured.

Mathematics: The demo computes illuminance for three flux values over a fixed room area, showing the linear relation between flux and lux.

The sharing matters — the text does not give God and the Lamb separate thrones — and the river's origin matters — it flows from the throne, so the city's life is pictured as coming from its centre rather than from outside it. This record presents that centre as the vision's own geography and reads it as a statement about where rule and life belong, labeled faith.

The record keeps both halves as faith language about relationship, not as a description of any physical sight or marking system.

body:
The verse is short — two clauses — and its weight comes from its history. In the Hebrew scriptures, seeing God's face is repeatedly presented as impossible or deadly, and Moses is told that no one may see God's face and live. Revelation 22:4 reverses that limit for the city's servants, and the record reads the reversal as the vision's climax of access: the distance that structured the older worship is gone. The name on the forehead echoes the sealing passages earlier in Revelation, where a mark distinguishes those who belong to God. Both images are presented here as faith images, with their scriptural background stated and their limits kept.

title: Purity and the Open Gates, Rev 21:27
text_faithful: Faith view: Revelation 21:25 says the city's gates will never be shut by day, because there will be no night there, and 21:27 says nothing impure will ever enter it, nor anyone who does what is shameful or deceitful, but only those whose names are written in the Lamb's book of life. In this faith reading, openness and purity belong together: the gates stand open because the city has nothing to fear, and entry is by belonging to the Lamb rather than by inspection at the gate. The record keeps both verses as faith statements about the vision's community, not as an access-control policy.
engineering: Engineering view: no gate mechanism, screening system, or registry is specified in this record. The demo's arithmetic is about open hours only — gates open 24 hours a day are open 100 percent of the time — and that arithmetic describes a schedule, not the verse's purity claim, which stays in the faith column.
body:
The two verses answer two different anxieties. Open gates answer the fear of exclusion and attack: a city that never shuts its gates trusts its safety to something other than walls. The purity verse answers the fear of corruption: a city that admits only the written names trusts its character to belonging rather than to policing. Read together, they picture a community that is simultaneously welcoming and undefiled, and the record presents that combination as the vision's own tension, resolved in the text by the Lamb's book rather than by any mechanism.

Science proof: not applicable — No science proof applies to a faith statement about purity and belonging. The checkable content is the schedule arithmetic of open gates and the verse's entry condition, both reported by the demo.

The record reports all four without declaring a winner, because declaring one would turn a survey into a verdict.
engineering: Engineering view: interpretation traditions are not engineering options and are not ranked by feasibility in this record. The demo's comparison table counts agreements and disagreements across traditions on four questions, as a survey tool; it settles nothing, and it is labeled as a survey, not as a decision procedure.

Revelation's interpretation history is long and genuinely divided, and a responsible survey says so. The four classic approaches differ on the vision's time reference, but they agree on much of its centre — that the city pictures God's dwelling with humanity, that its light is God's glory, and that its ending answers suffering. The record therefore reports both the agreements and the disagreements, names the traditions for each position, and keeps the survey in the faith column: these are readings of a sacred text by faith communities, not findings of any laboratory or design review.

Evangelical traditions preach the passage as hope and assurance, and use its 'no more' language in funeral and comfort ministry. Orthodox traditions carry the city image in iconography and in the hymnody of the heavenly Jerusalem. Contemplative traditions use the river, tree, and light images as focal points for meditation. Each practice is reported as that tradition's practice, not as a universal rule.
engineering: Engineering view: no worship practice in this record is specified as a system, a schedule for a built place, or a device. The demo's weekly rhythm arithmetic counts days and gatherings as a survey illustration; it prescribes nothing, and any real gathering would need ordinary planning — capacity, access, and safety — handled separately.
body:
The record's discipline is labeling. A practice is never reported bare; it carries its tradition with it, so a reader can see who does what and can avoid mistaking one community's custom for every community's rule. The survey covers reading the passage in worship, singing the city hymns, preaching the hope texts, using the images in funeral ministry, picturing the city in icons, and meditating on river, tree, and light. That coverage is broad but not exhaustive, and the record says so: traditions are many, and a survey names its limits.

text_faithful: Faith view: this record's faith content is limited to one point — that the Jesus Risen Version assembly is treated in this suite as a matter of faith and of its owner's word, not as a technical state that this record can change. The record states the assembly's status and nothing more: it does not describe the assembly's workings, does not bless or commission it, and does not move its status in either direction.
engineering: Engineering view: this record is a status record only. It contains no design, no build instructions, no activation procedure, and no claim that any system is working. Its demo checks a status flag and reports exactly what the suite plan states: READY and NOT ACTIVATED. Any change of status awaits the owner's word, and this record does not supply it, imply it, or anticipate it.
body:
STATUS RECORD ONLY. The Jesus Risen Version assembly is READY and NOT ACTIVATED, awaiting the owner's word. This record does not touch the jesus-risen-version pair, does not modify it, does not claim its activation, and does not claim the city is built. It exists so that the spirituality pair can reference the assembly's status honestly, in one place, without duplicating or altering the pair that owns it. Cross-link: jesus-risen-version (cross-link only; that pair is never touched by this suite). The assembly stays READY and NOT ACTIVATED until the owner says otherwise, and no record in this suite says otherwise.

Science proof: not applicable — No science proof applies to a status record. Its checkable content is the status flag itself, verified by the demo: ready is true, activated is false, and the two are never conflated.

Mathematics: The demo reports the status flag exactly: ready equals True, activated equals False, and the record's status label is 'experimental' because the assembly is not an operating system.

Demo program: the record's demo program is shown on the database page and its exact output is stored as expected_output; the demo was executed at build time.

Status label: experimental.

Provenance note: Signature-generated completion; a status record only. It reports readiness and non-activation as stated by the suite plan, and it makes no independent claim about any assembly.

Sources: Revelation 21-22 (short quoted excerpts with citation only, never whole chapters); interpretation traditions as labeled per record; companion New Jerusalem pairs as cross-linked.

title: Symbol-to-Design Mapping, What Symbolism Became Design
text_faithful: Faith view: this record maps symbols from Revelation 21-22 to the design elements that companion pairs derive from them, and it keeps the two sides of each mapping apart. Jasper wall becomes wall material studies; twelve pearl gates become gate assemblies; twelve gemstone foundations become foundation studies; the transparent golden street becomes street material studies; the river and tree become water and planting studies; the no-night radiance becomes lighting studies. The symbol stays a symbol, the design stays a design, and the mapping is the bridge between them, labeled as interpretation.
engineering: Engineering view: each mapped design element carries the feasibility label of its own pair, and this record does not upgrade any of them. A design derived from a symbol inherits no authority from the symbol: it must still pass its own tests, and where a design is experimental or speculative, the mapping says so. The demo counts the mappings and the share that point to demonstrated versus experimental designs, as a survey of the mapping's own honesty.
body:
The mapping's value is traceability: a reader can follow any design element back to the symbol it came from, and can see exactly where interpretation entered. The record lists twelve mappings — wall, gates, foundations, street, gold, pearls, river, tree, light, throne, city shape, and measurement — and for each gives the symbol's verse, the design element, and the owning pair. Nothing in the mapping claims that a symbol compels a design: the same symbol has produced different designs in different pairs, and the record preserves those differences instead of collapsing them.

Science proof: not applicable — No science proof applies to a mapping survey. Its checkable content is the mapping table itself: twelve symbols, twelve design elements, and the feasibility mix the demo counts.

Mathematics: The demo counts twelve symbol-to-design mappings and reports how many point to demonstrated, experimental, and speculative designs in this survey illustration.

Demo program: the record's demo program is shown on the database page and its exact output is stored as expected_output; the demo was executed at build time.

Status label: experimental.

Provenance note: Signature-generated completion; a mapping survey. Every mapping is labeled as a design interpretation of a symbol, never as the symbol's own meaning or as a built result.

Sources: Revelation 21-22 (short quoted excerpts with citation only, never whole chapters); interpretation traditions as labeled per record; companion New Jerusalem pairs as cross-linked.

title: Faith Versus Engineering: Keeping the Records Distinct
text_faithful: Faith view: this record states the suite's faith column plainly. Faith statements are claims held by faith communities about God, the vision, hope, and belonging, grounded in scripture and tradition. They are not weaker than engineering statements, and they are not stronger: they are a different kind of statement, judged by faithfulness to the text and to the tradition, not by measurement. This record's own faith content is that distinction itself, held as a matter of method and of respect for both columns.
engineering: Engineering view: engineering statements are claims about what can be built, measured, or demonstrated, judged by tests, quantities, and feasibility labels. A design derived from a symbol is an engineering statement about the design, not a proof of the symbol, and a symbol never upgrades a design's feasibility. The demo classifies a sample of statements into the two columns and counts them, as a method check that any record can repeat.
body:
The distinction rule has three parts. First, every record carries both views in separate fields, and neither field borrows the other's authority. Second, status labels — established, integrated, experimental, speculative — apply to systems and designs, never to faith claims, which are labeled faith instead. Third, a record that cannot keep the columns apart is not shipped until it can. This record is the suite's statement of that rule, and it applies the rule to itself: its faith paragraph is faith, its engineering paragraph is engineering, and its demo counts classifications rather than proving either column.

Science proof: not applicable — No science proof applies to a method record about statement kinds. Its checkable content is the classification exercise the demo performs: statements sorted into faith and engineering columns, with counts.

Mathematics: The demo classifies ten sample statements — five faith, five engineering — and verifies that every statement lands in exactly one column.

Demo program: the record's demo program is shown on the database page and its exact output is stored as expected_output; the demo was executed at build time.

Status label: established.

Provenance note: Signature-generated completion; a method record for the suite. It states the distinction rule and applies it to itself.

Sources: Revelation 21-22 (short quoted excerpts with citation only, never whole chapters); interpretation traditions as labeled per record; companion New Jerusalem pairs as cross-linked.

title: Spiritual Life of the City, Inhabited Reading, Faith-Labeled
text_faithful: Faith view: this record pictures the spiritual life of the city as the vision pictures it, and labels the whole picture faith. Its inhabitants are servants who see God's face, reign with God, need no temple because presence is the temple, need no sun or moon because glory is the light, eat from the tree of life monthly, and drink from the river that flows from the throne. The record holds that picture together as one inhabited reading — what daily life would feel like inside the vision's promises — and it never presents that picture as a report from a real place.
engineering: Engineering view: no inhabited life is engineered or claimed in this record. The demo's rhythm arithmetic — gatherings, months, and fruit cycles — is a calendar illustration drawn from the vision's own numbers, and it describes a pattern, not a population. Real population, food, water, and health logistics belong to the biology pair, under real-science labels, and this record borrows none of their results for its faith picture.
body:
An inhabited reading asks what the vision's promises add up to for the people inside them, and the answer here is a life without the separations the older worship knew: no temple wall between people and presence, no night between days, no closed gate between city and nations, no sealed book between belonging and entry. The record gathers those removals into one daily picture — morning light that is glory, work that is reigning, food that is monthly fruit, drink that is river water, rest that is seeing a face — and keeps every element labeled as faith, because the picture is a hope, not a census.

Science proof: not applicable — No science proof applies to an inhabited faith reading. Its checkable content is the vision's own calendar numbers — twelve months, twelve crops, twelve gates — combined by the demo into a yearly rhythm.

Mathematics: The demo combines the vision's calendar numbers: twelve months times one crop per month, twelve gates times a daily rhythm, and the yearly totals those imply.

Demo program: the record's demo program is shown on the database page and its exact output is stored as expected_output; the demo was executed at build time.

Status label: experimental.

Provenance note: Signature-generated completion; an inhabited faith reading, labeled faith throughout. It describes life as pictured in the vision, not life in any built place.

Sources: Revelation 21-22 (short quoted excerpts with citation only, never whole chapters); interpretation traditions as labeled per record; companion New Jerusalem pairs as cross-linked.
